plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: Wild poinsettias grow as tall shrubs in the dry forests of southern Mexico. In late December they carry fiery crimson bracts, which are leaves that look like petals. These surround clusters of tiny yellow flowers. The bright bracts are the plant's way of attracting pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through winter (roughly November to February) in its native range
plants.location: Southern Mexico, including Guerrero and Oaxaca, and widely grown in warm climates around the world
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used its sap to make a reddish dye and as a traditional medicine. Poinsettias flower in short days, so they bloom around Christmas.

plants.name: Delosperma cooperi
plants.description: Southern Africa is in midsummer in late December. Succulent mats of this ice plant are covered in glossy, daisy-like magenta flowers that open wide in full sun and close in dull weather.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, roughly November to March in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Eastern Cape and Free State of South Africa and Lesotho, and also grown in gardens in Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: The flowers look like they are covered in tiny ice crystals. Those shimmering surface cells hold water and help the plant survive drought.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: This coastal evergreen clings to cliffs and beaches. In December it becomes a mass of crimson pompom flowers made of long, bristly stamens, which draw nectar-loving birds such as tūī and bellbirds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer, peaking in December
plants.location: Coastal North Island of New Zealand
plants.funFact: Its flowering peaks around Christmas, so New Zealanders call it the Christmas tree. Some individual trees are hundreds of years old.
